title: Create registration and handoff functions for "event" dissectors
description:
Have make-regs.py look for "event prefixed" functions to determine if they should be called at (Stratoshark) startup during registration.

This removes the need for epan_supports_packets(), so it and its related functionality was removed.

marked this merge request as **ready**
@martin.r.mathieson - Does this new "event function registration naming" require any updates to the Python scripts (that may be looking at the registration and handoff routines of dissectors)?

I like the overall aim of this change, and the obvious necessary script change was what you already made to make-regs.py

Maybe there were some API usage (which columns are referenced maybe?) that heavily suggest intended use in one build or the other - we could use the presence/absence of the event_register function as a guide as to whether it looks right/consistent?  There may also be future divergence, e.g., new categories of expert item that clearly only apply to processes rather than protocols?

I should probably make tools/check_static.py check symbols use against both libraries (depending upon which builds they will be in), though considering being in both libraries may complicate fixing identified issues (e.g., only called by a Wireshark-only dissector).  I probably should already update it to check for whether referenced symbols are declared with WS_DLL_PUBLIC, and also whether they are now/still listed in epan/dissectors/CMakeLists.txt since we started being more selective..

Can't think of other changes needed for now.

I made sure checkAPI.pl is still run on the "event dissectors" (that was part of !22661), and I thought that covered most of it.  But if something is looking for "proto_register_*" or "proto_reg_handoff_*" that needs to be updated to catch "event dissector" hf_ item issues. A quick scan of check_static.py does look like there need to be changes to handle Stratoshark/event dissectors, but I'll leave that for a separate MR as I don't think this MR requires it, it just makes it easier to identify "event dissectors" and that they aren't required for Wireshark APIs.

I'm sure there is nothing immediate that will cause the pipeline to fail, but I can imagine soon adding a function to check_common.py to ask which libraries a dissector will be part of.

check_spelling.py does check for proto_register_protocol() in order to dynamically add the protocol name to the dictionary, but that is unaffected by this change.
